stat_summary: On 30 September 2025, 76.4% of staff directly employed by NHS Wales were female. Men were in the majority in two staff groups: ambulance staff (57% male) and medical and dental staff (53% male), according to official Welsh Government figures.
stat_source_title: NHS workforce: staff directly employed by NHS Wales, 30 September 2025, Welsh Government

male.headline: The Night Shift Nobody Flags: Men Are 57 Per Cent of Ambulance Staff, and the Siren Is the Only Applause They Get
male.standfirst: New official figures confirm what every paramedic already knows from a wet forecourt at 2am: men are doing the majority of the ambulance graft, and getting precious little credit for the part of the NHS that arrives first.
male.image_caption: Owen, 38, between jobs. The kettle in the cab has packed up.
body_paragraphs: New official figures have confirmed what every paramedic already knows from a wet forecourt at 2am: men are doing the majority of the ambulance graft. Fifty-seven per cent of ambulance staff in NHS Wales are male – one of only two staff groups in which men outnumber women – and they receive, in return, precious little credit for the part of the service that actually arrives first.

“I stood in the rain for twenty minutes with the back doors open and a radio that would not shut up,” said Owen, 38, from Swansea. “A passer-by asked if we were filming something. Nobody offered to fetch a cup of tea.”

The same official release shows men are also a slight majority among medical and dental staff, at 53 per cent, even while they are a clear minority of the workforce as a whole. Campaigners are already calling for a National First-On-Scene Day, and for a reserved parking space at every hospital for crews who are, in their words, “just trying to get the job in”.
Yet where is the outrage? Where is the documentary? Britain's unsung night shift closes the doors, alone, with only the siren for company.
male.pull_quote: A passer-by asked if we were filming something. Nobody offered to fetch a cup of tea.

female.headline: She Is the NHS: 76 Per Cent of the Workforce Is Female, and They're Still Holding the Place Together
female.standfirst: Official figures have finally put a number on who actually staffs the health service, and it does not look anything like a brief appearance in a drama.
female.image_caption: Ffion, 44, end of shift. The tea is the first sitting-down of the day.
body_paragraphs: Official figures have at last put a number on who actually staffs the health service. On 30 September 2025, 76.4 per cent of staff directly employed by NHS Wales were women, which means that, in any honest reading, they are not helping to run the NHS. They are the NHS.

“He did a 12-hour shift and talked about it all weekend,” said Ffion, 44, from Cardiff. “I have done five in a row, missed the kettle twice and still have the handover to write, and nobody's named a ward after me.”

The same statistics show women making up the overwhelming majority of the service even as men predominate in a couple of high-visibility groups. Campaigners are demanding a Handover Act of Thanks and a national apology for the phrase “the nurses will deal with that”.
Until then, the country's unofficial backbone will keep the bay moving, one lukewarm cup of tea at a time.
female.pull_quote: I have done five in a row, missed the kettle twice and still have the handover to write, and nobody's named a ward after me.
